decisions.place: Top-centre manuscript page number and flanking strokes
decisions.scan_shows: A low short freehand dash stands to the left of the open-topped, looped 6; a second, longer and darker horizontal stroke stands to its right. All three have continuous pen-like contours; the dashes are separate visible marks, not inferred punctuation.

decisions.place: Opening cancelled word before live mis
decisions.scan_shows: Three typed letters remain under three crossing x impressions: the first has the two humps and low legs of m, the middle has a separate i dot above the cancellation, and the last retains the lower-left curl and right curve of s. The next, uncancelled mis is separately visible in the half. C-context target confirmed.

decisions.place: p.22, li.5: covered last page-reference character
decisions.scan_shows: The composite character contains a rounded upper-right turn and a diagonal/flat foot compatible with the live 2. Additional nearly straight top and bottom bars have a short downward terminal at the upper left and an upward terminal at the lower right; those terminal spurs suggest the typed Z shape seen in the dimension formula. A covered 3 or a displaced repeated 2 remains possible because the central and lower curves merge. Z is therefore added as the preferred uncertain underprint; this changes the recorded alternatives, not merely the macro syntax. The exact chronological order of overlapping impressions is not independently recoverable.

One continuous narrow stroke begins with a rounded dark left end, rises slightly through its middle, and tapers into a faint right end just before the p. C represents it by a textual em dash; the observed slight arch, tapered end, and left-of-reference placement are instead preserved in a drawing. The difference is the observed contour, not the change of macro alone.

decisions.place: p.24, li.11: detached marks after et
decisions.scan_shows: Two distinct dark marks survive: the lower-left one is a small horizontal oval, and the upper-right one is narrower and obliquely elongated. Their centres differ in both x and y, and both lie above the prose baseline. They do not have the vertically aligned, equal-size construction of the typed colons in the references. The physical pair is retained by its shape and position; intentional punctuation versus incidental marks is unresolved.

decisions.place: p.25, li.8: cancelled word after Répétition
decisions.scan_shows: Eleven typewriter x impressions cover the word. Surviving features include initial m legs, an a bowl, the tall hooked l, partial curves at the s position, the closed o, closely spaced n uprights, a later rounded a bowl, the tall t and crossbar, and a final e loop/bar. The x strokes obscure several joins, especially the s and middle sequence, so malsonnante remains a marked reading rather than a certain recovery.

inventory.element: Archive sheet number, recorded as comment

notes: One typescript sheet, with manuscript page number - 6 - at the top and archive sheet number 70 at the lower left. There is no title, date, letterhead, signature, stamp, or separate displayed diagram. The page contains an opening continuation paragraph and twenty page-and-line comments, spanning references to pages 18–25. H is description-only and unavailable as a transcription; h_reading is null and diff_h is false throughout. The text records editorial deletions, spelling corrections, requests for references, missing arrows, and suggested hypotheses. Explicit author questions ask whether a claim needs more hypotheses on Z, whether linéairement means rationnellement, whether f should be assumed smooth, what hypotheses on X are needed, whether the corollary should be supplied for NS, and for references for essentially finite type and universally Japanese. It says that the Gr comparison modulo torsion is used implicitly, requests a reference for the equality of dimensions, says to suppose X flat over S, and regrets the absence of a proof. Those are the page's statements; no proof or background theorem was checked. The spaces after VII and SGA 5 IV are blank and remain blank. Quoted standard/standart and rationnelle/rationelle, the literal quoted ellipses, and the absence of a final full stop after the last closing quotation are retained. All C-context places were inspected. The cancelled opening mis, the quoted spelling pairs, the live reference 22, the t under the first n of donne, and the main live words are confirmed. Five explicit C doubts are accounted for: the page-reference underprint gains Z as a preferred alternative; the detached pair is reproduced as a graphic with unresolved function; e/a in donne remains; m under démonstration is resolved; and malsonnante remains uncertain. Reference numerals and mathematical indices were checked individually for material state; their repeated glyph forms and typewriter impressions support typed construction, while the page-number group, Gr arrow/tilde and two marginal strokes are handwritten. The small pair after et has unresolved origin. Its drawing is therefore not used to assert an authorial punctuation intention.
math_reading_decisions: The p.19 statement reads \mathrm{Gr}^{\bullet}\handwritten{\xrightarrow{\sim}}\mathrm{Gr}^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{top}} modulo torsion. Both exponents are filled points above the baseline; top is a lowered, typed t-o-p. The arrow has one long shaft with a right-facing hand-drawn head and a separate single wavy tilde above it.

The dimension equality is exactly \dim(Z_s) = \dim(Z_t). The lowered s has two opposing curves and the lowered t has a stem and crossbar; both are typed. There are two horizontal equality strokes and ordinary single-outline Z capitals.

The isolated Z, S, X and f in the prose are ordinary typed characters. NS consists of ordinary upright typed capitals; the last entry has S with one raised prime in its first quoted phrase and plain S in the second.
XIV 5.1 et 5.2, V 3.3.2, VII, SGA 5 IV, EGA IV 2.8, cf. IV 2.12 and EGA II 7.1.9 were read as written. The Roman capitals have single typewriter outlines and no manuscript over/under-rules.

Every page-and-line numeral group was inspected for construction. The 1 forms have flat feet and leftward top heads like the typed l; the 2 forms have a recurring curved head and flat foot; the 3 forms have a flat head, angled neck and broad lower curve; 4 is open-topped; 5, 6, 7, 8 and 9 recur with consistent typewriter contours. No handwritten wrapper was added to these numerical references. The overprinted last digit in p.22 li.5 is separately marked uncertain.
The final S prime is a single raised apostrophe-like stroke; the following two high quotation strokes are separate. It is not an exclamation mark or a second mathematical prime.
The mathematical text was used only to locate and distinguish glyphs. No claim was proved, calculated, or checked against external background.

completion: Full diplomatic coverage completed: all text paragraphs, accents, spelling, punctuation, reference numerals, inline mathematics, manuscript pagination, archive number, cancellations/overprints, handwritten arrow, and three detached graphical elements are transcribed or recorded. The whole source and halves a then b were viewed once each; all 35 listed tight crops were viewed once each and retained. No OCR, web research, other-page images, peer-reader files, delegation, proof checking, or TeX compilation was used. Post-save structural checks passed: balanced braces, math delimiters and environments; all decision bboxes and retained crop paths validated. No compilation was attempted.
